title: Python Modules and Safe Files
description: Practice standard-library imports, the main guard, and the basic idea of reading files with a context manager.

questions.prompt: What does import math make available?
options: The math module under the name math
The names from math without a module prefix
Every function in math runs immediately
A local file named math is created
questions.correct: The math module under the name math
questions.explanation: After import math, code can use names such as math.sqrt and math.pi.
math.sqrt returns the square root as a floating-point value, so the result displays as 4.0.

questions.prompt: The main guard prevents main() from running when the file is imported as a module.
questions.explanation: if __name__ == '__main__' is true when the file is run directly, not when it is imported for tests.

questions.prompt: Which form imports sqrt directly from math?
questions.explanation: from module import name brings the selected name into the current module.

options: It closes the file automatically when the block ends
It reads the entire file automatically
It changes the file to read-only
questions.correct: It closes the file automatically when the block ends
questions.explanation: A context manager cleans up the file even when the block exits because of an error.

questions.code:
from pathlib import Path
path = Path('notes.txt')
print(path.suffix)
questions.explanation: Path.suffix is the file extension, including the leading dot.

questions.prompt: Which mode opens a file for reading text?
questions.explanation: r means read. w writes and can replace existing contents; a appends.

questions.prompt: A module is another Python file whose functions and values can be imported.
questions.explanation: Modules let a program organize reusable code across files.
When run directly, the main guard calls run and prints its returned value.

questions.prompt: What is the safest place for a lesson's generated output file?
options: The user's home directory regardless of the assignment
questions.explanation: Keeping files inside the workspace makes the program portable and respects the runner's isolation boundary.
